Compared to 10 Years Ago, USA is Losing Competitiveness

at the Margin vs. lts Peers

e McKinsey conducted a study in 2010 that compares the USA with other countries on 20 attributes related to economic fundamentals, business climate, human capital and infrastructure. McKinsey compared current status vs. status in 2000.

e We augmented the McKinsey study with 9 additional attributes across those aforementioned areas as well as government spending metrics.

e Through this study, we found that America, relative to other countries, improved on none of the 29 attributes, remained the same on 9 attributes (including GDP per capita, public debt as % of GDP, public spending on healthcare, public spending on education, growth in local innovation clusters, population &
demographic profile, retention of foreign-born talents, total healthcare spending and cost-adjusted labor productivity) and deteriorated on 20 (including trade surplus, national spending on R&D, industrial production, corporate tax rate, business environment, FDI, tax incentives for R&D, number of patent
applications, availability of high-quality labor, higher education penetration, telecom & transportation infrastructure, etc.).
